A right-hander's conductive jacket therefore does not conform on a left-hander (see also t.64.4). Non-conforming clothing or equipment is a first group offence: a yellow card the first time, and the fencer must obtain regulation equipment within 5 minutes (t.71; t.75.1).

choices: Award a hit for X but give him a yellow card
Cancel the hit and punish X with a yellow card
Award a hit for Y and punish X with a yellow card
SAB-004.explain: At sabre it is forbidden to hit with the guard: the hit is annulled and the offence is in the first group (t.96.3; t.170 item 1.12), a yellow card the first time and a red card if the fencer already has a yellow in the bout (t.165). Fencer X's action is still the attack, so Fencer Y's counter attack into it was not in time (a stop hit into a simple attack, t.106.3.a) and Fencer Y's hit is not awarded. With no hit awarded, the fencers are replaced where the bout was interrupted (t.22.7).

choices: Annul both hits as a simultaneous action; no penalty is given because there was no brutality involved
Yellow card for Fencer X, Fencer X's hit annulled, and the hit awarded to Fencer Y, whose attack was properly executed
Yellow card for Fencer X and Fencer X's hit annulled; the attacks were simultaneous, so no hit is awarded
SAB-005.explain: A hit made with the guard is forbidden at sabre even when no brutality is involved: it is annulled and the offence is in the first group, a yellow card the first time and a red card if it happens again in the bout (t.96.3; t.165). Both fencers attacked simultaneously, so neither had priority (t.106.1), and Fencer Y's hit is not awarded either. The fencers are replaced where the bout was interrupted (t.22.7).

SAB-006.explain: A point in line only obliges the attacker to deflect it if it was established before the attack began (t.102.1). Here the attack starts first, so it is properly executed (arm straightening precedes the lunge, t.101.3-4) and must be parried or avoided. The fencer who is attacked and makes a stop hit is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.a). Fencer Y has committed no offence by extending the arm after the command.

choices: Do not award the hit and punish X with a red card: score 4:4
Award a hit for X and punish him with a red card: Fencer X wins the bout 5:4
Award a hit for Y and punish X with a red card: Fencer Y wins the bout 4:5
SAB-007.explain: The fleche, or any forward movement in which the rear foot passes the front foot, is forbidden at sabre. The hit of the fencer at fault is annulled, but any hit correctly executed by the opponent is valid (t.101.5). Fencer X already has a yellow card, so a further first group offence in the same bout is a red card (t.165). Fencer Y therefore receives a hit plus the penalty hit: 3 + 1 + 1 = 5, against 4 for Fencer X.

SAB-008.explain: The maximum length of the sabre blade is 88 cm. 105 cm is the maximum total length of the whole sabre ready for use (m.21, m.23.1).

SAB-009.explain: The blade may have a distinct, continuous curve whose deflection is less than 4 cm, measured as the greatest distance between the blade and a flat surface when the blade lies with the curve uppermost. Blades with sharply bent extremities, or that curve in the direction of the cutting edge, are forbidden (m.23.3). This is separate from the flexibility test, a bend of 4 to 7 cm under a 200 g weight (m.23.4).

choices: should be long enough to assure the electrical contact between the electric jacket and the mask
must be between 30 cm and 40 cm long
must be longer than 40 cm and can be coiled
SAB-010.explain: The electrical contact between the mask and the conductive jacket is made by a white or clear-covered wire between 30 cm and 40 cm long, with a crocodile clip at each end, soldered to the wire. A coiled mask wire is not allowed, and the resistance of the wire between the clips must not exceed 1 ohm (m.32.4-5).

choices: Annul Fencer X's hit and give Fencer X a red card (second group, penalty hit) for the dangerous blow with the guard
Award Fencer X's hit and then give Fencer X a red card, because the blow came after the hit had been scored
Annul Fencer X's hit and give Fencer X a yellow card, because the blow with the guard is a first group offence like a hit with the guard
SAB-011.explain: A dangerous, violent or vindictive action, including a blow struck with the guard, is a second group offence: a red card (penalty hit) every time, and any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled (t.121.2; t.166; t.170 item 2.6). The blow follows the hit in one continuous action, so the hit is connected with the offence and is annulled with it (t.161).

choices: award a hit for Y; X receives a YELLOW CARD
no hit awarded; X receives a YELLOW CARD.
SAB-012.explain: A fleche or any forward movement in which the rear foot passes the front foot is forbidden at sabre. The hit of the fencer at fault is annulled and any hit correctly executed by the opponent is valid (t.101.5), so Fencer Y's hit counts when it arrived in the same fencing time. With no earlier penalties in the bout it is a first offence in the first group, so a yellow card (t.165; t.170 item 1.12).

choices: that the conductive jacket covers the complete torso
that the conductive jacket must overlap the breeches by at least 5cm when in the on guard position
that the jacket must cover the valid surface and the sleeves must be fixed at the wrist by an elastic band
SAB-013.explain: Before the bout the referee checks that the FIE guarantee label is present on the equipment (t.64.1) and that the sabre conductive jacket conforms to m.34 with the fencer on guard (t.64.4): the conductive surface must cover entirely and without omission the valid target above the horizontal line joining the tops of the hip bones, and the arms as far as the wrists (m.34.1-2).

SAB-014.explain: Intentionally dropping the weapon during the fencing phrase is a second group offence: red card (penalty hit). The opponent's hit is valid provided the action was started before 'Halt!' (t.56.11; t.170 item 2.4). Fencer Y's immediate riposte was already under way, so Fencer Y gets the hit and the penalty hit.

choices: a seizing of the attacker’s blade.
an immediate new attack after return to guard.
a reply to the attack in an indirect or delayed action.
SAB-015.explain: The reprise of the attack is a new attack executed immediately after a return to the on-guard position (t.13.3). The first option is the remise (t.13.1), the second is the redoublement (t.13.2) and the last is counter-time (t.13.4).

choices: confiscate X’s weapon; X receives a YELLOW CARD .
confiscate X’s weapon; X receives a RED CARD .
confiscate X’s weapon; no additional penalty required.
SAB-016.explain: Equipment found on the piste to be non-regulation or defective is confiscated and sent to the experts (t.70). When the irregularity found during a bout could have been caused by conditions during the bout, the referee applies neither warning nor penalty, and any hit scored with equipment that has become defective is awarded (t.72). The yellow card does not change this, because no offence has been committed. Fencer X continues with a regulation weapon.

choices: Give the command “Allez!”, but do not award any hit scored by X’s existing line.
Instruct X to remove the line.
SAB-017.explain: At foil and sabre the fencers may not come on guard in the 'in line' position (t.22.13), and they must come on guard correctly and stay still until the command is given (t.22.12). No movement made before the command counts (t.23.1). The referee therefore has Fencer X come on guard correctly before starting the bout. A first group penalty only follows if Fencer X refuses to obey the referee (t.112; t.170 item 1.13).

choices: Award a hit for Fencer X. Fencer Y must replace weapon.
Confiscate the illegal weapon; Y receives a yellow card; require Y to get a legal weapon.
SAB-018.explain: If the sabre of the fencer judged to have been hit does not conform to m.24.6-8 (insulation of the interior and exterior of the guard, the handle and the pommel), there is no annulment, even if the hit on the weapon causes a signal to register (t.99.2). Fencer X's hit stands. Fencer Y still has to correct the weapon.

SAB-019.explain: The conductive material of the glove must be turned over into the inside of the gauntlet to a depth of at least 5 cm (m.33.2).

choices: Have the fencer tie hair so that it does not conceal the name on the back. Covering target with hair above the name and below the collar of the lame is allowed.
Give Fencer X a YELLOW CARD and the fencer must arrange the hair so that it does not cover the lame at all.
SAB-020.explain: Before the start of the bout the hair must be fastened and placed inside the clothing and/or mask so that it does not cover a valid surface, does not hide the name and nationality, and does not need to be put back during the bout. Violation is a first group offence (t.115.2; t.170 item 1.14): a yellow card the first time.

choices: Do not award a hit and X receives a YELLOW CARD.
SAB-021.explain: Any forward movement in which the rear foot passes the front foot is forbidden at sabre: the referee halts the bout (t.23.5) and the offence is in the first group, a yellow card the first time (t.101.5; t.165; t.170 item 1.12). Fencer Y's stop-cut was the action made within the fencing time and it missed. Nothing started after the halt counts (t.23.3), so the remises are not counted at all. No hit is awarded, and the fencers are replaced where the bout was halted (t.22.7).

SAB-022.explain: If, when trying to find the opponent's blade to deflect it, the attacker does not find it (derobement), the right of attack passes to the opponent (t.102.2). The attacker who attempts to find the blade, fails, and continues is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.b). Fencer X gets the hit.

choices: Ask Fencer X to change the over-glove.
Confiscate the illegal over-glove; X receives a YELLOW CARD; require X to get a legal over-glove.
SAB-023.explain: The glove must have an elastic band, a popper button or another approved system to guarantee contact with the jacket sleeve (m.33.3). Non-regulation equipment on the piste is confiscated (t.70). Non-conforming clothing or equipment is a first group offence: a yellow card the first time, and the fencer must obtain regulation equipment in no more than 5 minutes (t.71; t.170 item 1.8).

choices: When the attacker touches the opponent's blade, even lightly, before starting the lunge
When the attacker first beats or takes the opponent's blade; mere contact is not enough
Always, because an attack takes precedence over a point in line
SAB-024.explain: If the attack is initiated when the opponent has a point in line, the attacker must first deflect the opponent's blade, by a beat or by taking the blade. Referees must ensure that a mere contact of the blades is not considered sufficient (t.102.1). Without that, the attacker alone is counted as hit (t.106.4.a). Likewise the fencer in line who, after being beaten or taken, attacks or replaces the point in line instead of parrying is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.e).

choices: Only when the opponent's hit actually lands on the substituted area
Only when the judges confirm it; the referee cannot decide this alone
When it occurs during the fencing phrase, whether or not a hit lands there
SAB-025.explain: At sabre it is forbidden to protect the target area or substitute another part of the body for it by covering it. If this happens during the fencing phrase, any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled and the offence is in the first group, whether or not the opponent's hit lands there (t.97.2; t.30.1; t.170 item 1.4).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer X, because Fencer X made the parry and the renewed attack came too late
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because the lights came on together
Award the hit to Fencer Y: the delayed riposte gave Fencer Y the right to renew the attack
SAB-026.explain: The fencer who, after a successful parry, makes a momentary pause (delayed riposte) which gives the opponent the right to renew the attack is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.c). Only an immediate, simple riposte annuls the attacker's later actions (t.105.1).

SAB-027.explain: Fencer X had the point in line before Fencer Y started to attack, so Fencer Y had to deflect the blade first (t.102.1). Fencer Y tried to find the blade but failed (derobement), so the right of attack passes to Fencer X (t.102.2). The attacker who does this and continues is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.a-b). This assumes Fencer X keeps the line and hits with the tip of the blade.

choices: Award the hit to Fencer Y: the beat on the forte gives the right to an immediate riposte
Award the hit to Fencer X, because a beat on the blade always keeps the priority of the attack
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because both landed at the same time
SAB-028.explain: A beat made on the forte (the third of the blade nearest the guard) means the attack is badly executed and gives the opponent the right to an immediate riposte. Only a beat on the foible (the two thirds furthest from the guard) keeps the attack's priority (t.104).

SAB-029.explain: A point in line only obliges the attacker to deflect it when it was established before the attack began (t.102.1). The attack started first and was correct (t.101.3-4); Fencer Y, as the fencer attacked, who makes a stop hit is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.a).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer X, because a compound attack always has priority over any riposte
Award the hit to Fencer Y, who found the blade during a feint and riposted immediately
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because they landed at the same time
SAB-030.explain: If, during a compound attack, the opponent finds the blade during one of the feints, the opponent has the right to riposte (t.103). The attacker who allows the opponent to find the blade and continues the attack while the opponent ripostes immediately is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.c).

SAB-031.explain: An attack with a step-forward-lunge is correctly carried out only if the hit arrives at the latest when the front foot hits the piste (t.101.4.a). Fencer X's hit arrived after the front foot hit the piste, so the attack had no priority and the hit of Fencer Y is awarded.

choices: at the discretion of the Referee
when both fencers are in a proper on guard position ‘point in line’, the points should not overlap
SAB-032.explain: When placed on guard during the bout, the distance between the two competitors must be such that, in the position point in line, the points of the two blades cannot make contact (t.22.5).

SAB-033.explain: Only a weapon dropped intentionally during the fencing phrase is an offence (t.56.11). A weapon that falls because of the beat is not, so the hit of Fencer X on the valid target is awarded.

SAB-034.explain: When a competitor against whom a hit has been registered has broken the blade, the hit must be annulled unless the breaking clearly occurred after the hit was registered (t.56.7). The blade of Fencer X broke during the action, so the hit of Fencer Y is annulled and no hit is awarded.

SAB-035.explain: A hit which arrives on a non-valid part of the target is not counted, is not registered by the apparatus, does not stop the fencing phrase and does not annul any subsequent hit (t.98). The valid hit of Fencer Y is therefore awarded.

SAB-036.explain: In a compound attack the opponent has the right to stop-hit, but to be valid the stop hit must arrive before the attacker has started the last movement (t.103). The hit of Fencer Y arrived at the same time as the last movement, so it was not in time: Fencer Y alone is counted as hit and the hit is awarded to Fencer X (t.106.3.d).
